Temperature controls the randomness in t: Temperature controls the randomness in token selection:- low temperature (<1.0) leads to more predictable text, favoring higher probability tokens.- high temperature (>1.0) increases creativity and diversity in the output by giving lower probability tokens a better chance.Set to 1.0 for the original probabilities.
Top_K_desc: Top K sets a maximum amount of top tokens that can be chosen from.E.g Top K is 20, this means only the 20 highest ranking tokens will be kept (regardless of their probabilities being diverse or limited).Set to 0 (or -1, depending on your backend) to disable.
Top_P_desc: Top P (a.k.a. nucleus sampling) adds up all the top tokens required to add up to the target percentage.E.g If the Top 2 tokens are both 25%, and Top P is 0.50, only the Top 2 tokens are considered.Set to 1.0 to disable.
Typical_P_desc: Typical P Sampling prioritizes tokens based on their deviation from the average entropy of the set.It maintains tokens whose cumulative probability is close to a predefined threshold (e.g., 0.5), emphasizing those with average information content.Set to 1.0 to disable.
Min_P_desc: Min P sets a base minimum probability. This is scaled according to the top token's probability.E.g If Top token is 80% probability, and Min P is 0.1, only tokens higher than 8% would be considered.Set to 0 to disable.
Top_A_desc: Top A sets a threshold for token selection based on the square of the highest token probability.E.g if the Top-A value is 0.2 and the top token's probability is 50%, tokens with probabilities below 5% (0.2 * 0.5^2) are excluded.Set to 0 to disable.
Tail_Free_Sampling_desc: Tail-Free Sampling (TFS) searches for a tail of low-probability tokens in the distribution,by analyzing the rate of change in token probabilities using derivatives. It retains tokens up to a threshold (e.g., 0.3) based on the normalized second derivative.The closer to 0, the more discarded tokens. Set to 1.0 to disable.

Epsilon cutoff sets a probability floor: Epsilon cutoff sets a probability floor below which tokens are excluded from being sampled.In units of 1e-4; a reasonable value is 3.Set to 0 to disable.
Eta_Cutoff_desc: Eta cutoff is the main parameter of the special Eta Sampling technique.In units of 1e-4; a reasonable value is 3.Set to 0 to disable.See the paper Truncation Sampling as Language Model Desmoothing by Hewitt et al. (2022) for details.
Smooth_Sampling_desc: Allows you to use quadratic/cubic transformations to adjust the distribution. Lower Smoothing Factor values will be more creative, usually between 0.2-0.3 is the sweetspot (assuming the curve = 1). Higher Smoothing Curve values will make the curve steeper, which will punish low probability choices more aggressively. 1.0 curve is equivalent to only using Smoothing Factor.
DRY_Repetition_Penalty_desc: DRY penalizes tokens that would extend the end of the input into a sequence that has previously occurred in the input. Set multiplier to 0 to disable.
DRY_Multiplier_desc: Set to value > 0 to enable DRY. Controls the magnitude of the penalty for the shortest penalized sequences.
DRY_Base_desc: Controls how fast the penalty grows with increasing sequence length.
DRY_Allowed_Length_desc: Longest sequence that can be repeated without being penalized.
DRY_Sequence_Breakers_desc: Tokens across which sequence matching is not continued. Specified as a comma-separated list of quoted strings.
Scale Temperature dynamically per token,: Scale Temperature dynamically per token, based on the variation of probabilities.
Mirostat_desc: Mirostat is a thermostat for output perplexity.Mirostat matches the output perplexity to that of the input, thus avoiding the repetition trap(where, as the autoregressive inference produces text, the perplexity of the output tends toward zero)and the confusion trap (where the perplexity diverges).For details, see the paper Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity by Basu et al. (2020).Mode chooses the Mirostat version. 0=disable, 1=Mirostat 1.0 (llama.cpp only), 2=Mirostat 2.0.Tau = Variability parameter for Mirostat outputs.Eta = Learning rate of Mirostat.

This is almost always the sensible thing to do.When enabled: sample the set of plausible tokens first, then apply temperature to adjust their relative probabilities (technically, logits).When disabled: apply temperature to adjust the relative probabilities of ALL tokens first, then sample plausible tokens from that.Disabling Temperature Last boosts the probabilities in the tail of the distribution, which tends to amplify the chances of getting an incoherent response.

Top K sets a maximum amount of top token: Top K sets a maximum amount of top tokens that can be chosen from.E.g Top K is 20, this means only the 20 highest ranking tokens will be kept (regardless of their probabilities being diverse or limited).Set to 0 (or -1, depending on your backend) to disable.
Top P (a.k.a. nucleus sampling) adds up: Top P (a.k.a. nucleus sampling) adds up all the top tokens required to add up to the target percentage.E.g If the Top 2 tokens are both 25%, and Top P is 0.50, only the Top 2 tokens are considered.Set to 1.0 to disable.
Typical P Sampling prioritizes tokens ba: Typical P Sampling prioritizes tokens based on their deviation from the average entropy of the set. Set to 1.0 to disable.
Min P sets a base minimum probability. T: Min P sets a base minimum probability. This is scaled according to the top token's probability.E.g If Top token is 80% probability, and Min P is 0.1, only tokens higher than 8% would be considered.Set to 0 to disable.
Top A sets a threshold for token selecti: Top A sets a threshold for token selection based on the square of the highest token probability.E.g if the Top-A value is 0.2 and the top token's probability is 50%, tokens with probabilities below 5% (0.2 * 0.5^2) are excluded.Set to 0 to disable.
Top K sets a maximum amount of top token: Top K sets a maximum amount of top tokens that can be chosen from.E.g Top K is 20, this means only the 20 highest ranking tokens will be kept (regardless of their probabilities being diverse or limited).Set to 0 to disable.
Typical P Sampling prioritizes tokens ba: Typical P Sampling prioritizes tokens based on their deviation from the average entropy of the set.It maintains tokens whose cumulative probability is close to a predefined threshold (e.g., 0.5), emphasizing those with average information content.Set to 1.0 to disable.
Min P sets a base minimum probability.\r: Min P sets a base minimum probability.This is scaled according to the top token's probability.E.g If Top token is 80% probability, and Min P is 0.1, only tokens higher than 8% would be considered.Set to 0 to disable.
Tail-Free Sampling (TFS) searches for a: Tail-Free Sampling (TFS) searches for a tail of low-probability tokens in the distribution,by analyzing the rate of change in token probabilities using derivatives. It retains tokens up to a threshold (e.g., 0.3) based on the normalized second derivative.The closer to 0, the more discarded tokens. Set to 1.0 to disable.
A value of 0 disables Mirostat entirely. 1 is for Mirostat 1.0, and 2 is for Mirostat 2.0
Ban the End-of-Sequence (EOS) token with: Ban the End-of-Sequence (EOS) token with KoboldCpp (and possibly also other tokens with KoboldAI).Good for story writing, but should not be used for chat and instruct mode.
Epsilon cutoff sets a probability floor: Epsilon cutoff sets a probability floor below which tokens are excluded from being sampled.In units of 1e-4; a reasonable value is 3.Set to 0 to disable.
A sampling method that filters logits ba: A sampling method that filters logits based on their statistical properties. It keeps tokens within n standard deviations of the maximum logit value, providing a simpler alternative to top-p/top-k sampling while maintaining sampling stability across different temperatures.
A sampling modifier that ensures that tr: A sampling modifier that ensures that truncation samplers such as top-p, min-p, typical-p, and xtc return at least this many tokens. Set to 0 to disable.
Eta cutoff is the main parameter of the: Eta cutoff is the main parameter of the special Eta Sampling technique.In units of 1e-4; a reasonable value is 3.Set to 0 to disable.See the paper Truncation Sampling as Language Model Desmoothing by Hewitt et al. (2022) for details.
Allows you to use quadratic/cubic transf: Allows you to use quadratic/cubic transformations to adjust the distribution. Lower Smoothing Factor values will be more creative, usually between 0.2-0.3 is the sweetspot (assuming the curve = 1). Higher Smoothing Curve values will make the curve steeper, which will punish low probability choices more aggressively. 1.0 curve is equivalent to only using Smoothing Factor.
DRY penalizes tokens that would extend t: DRY penalizes tokens that would extend the end of the input into a sequence that has previously occurred in the input. Set multiplier to 0 to disable.
Controls how fast the penalty grows with: Controls how fast the penalty grows with increasing sequence length.
Longest sequence that can be repeated wi: Longest sequence that can be repeated without being penalized.
Tokens across which sequence matching is: Tokens across which sequence matching is not continued. Specified as a comma-separated list of quoted strings.
Scale Temperature dynamically per token,: Scale Temperature dynamically per token, based on the variation of probabilities.
Mirostat is a thermostat for output perp: Mirostat is a thermostat for output perplexity.Mirostat matches the output perplexity to that of the input, thus avoiding the repetition trap(where, as the autoregressive inference produces text, the perplexity of the output tends toward zero)and the confusion trap (where the perplexity diverges).For details, see the paper Mirostat: A Neural Text Decoding Algorithm that Directly Controls Perplexity by Basu et al. (2020).Mode chooses the Mirostat version. 0=disable, 1=Mirostat 1.0 (llama.cpp only), 2=Mirostat 2.0.Tau = Variability parameter for Mirostat outputs.Eta = Learning rate of Mirostat.
A sampler that encourages diversity whil: A sampler that encourages diversity while maintaining coherence, by exploiting the isotropicity of the representation space of most LLMs. For details, see the paper A Contrastive Framework for Neural Text Generation by Su et al. (2022).
Strength of the Contrastive Search regul: Strength of the Contrastive Search regularization term. Set to 0 to disable CS.

Ban the eos_token. This forces the model: Ban the eos_token. This forces the model to never end the generation prematurely.
Use the temperature sampler last. This i: Use the temperature sampler last. This is almost always the sensible thing to do.When enabled: sample the set of plausible tokens first, then apply temperature to adjust their relative probabilities (technically, logits).When disabled: apply temperature to adjust the relative probabilities of ALL tokens first, then sample plausible tokens from that.Disabling Temperature Last boosts the probabilities in the tail of the distribution, which tends to amplify the chances of getting an incoherent response.
Use a different speculative decoding met: Use a different speculative decoding method without a draft model.Using a draft model is preferred. Speculative ngram is not as effective.
A random seed to use for deterministic a: A random seed to use for deterministic and reproducable outputs. Set to -1 to use a random seed.

Use token counter (with the correct tokenizer selected first!) if you are unsure.Enclose text in double quotes to ban the entire string as a set.Quoted Strings and [Token ids] must be on their own line.

**Add entry** makes a new, blank entry. Give each person, place or secret its own entry, so only the detail that matters joins the reply.
This book has no entries yet. Press **Ad: This book has no entries yet. Press **Add entry** now to make your first one, then press **Next**.
One big entry about everything is how yo: One big entry about everything is how you end up paying for tokens you never needed. Ask me how I know.
Press **Edit** on an entry to see what i: Press **Edit** on an entry to see what is inside it. Try it now, or press **Next** and I will open the first one.
The little switch beside it turns an ent: The little switch beside it turns an entry off without deleting it. Very handy for a secret that is not ready yet.
These are the **Primary Keywords**. Type: These are the **Primary Keywords**. Type a word and press Enter to add it: a name, a nickname, a place.
When any of them appears in the recent m: When any of them appears in the recent messages, this entry is added to what the model reads for its next reply.
Pick words people actually say. 'Mara' w: Pick words people actually say. 'Mara' works. 'The fishmonger with the tragic past' will never come up, trust me.

Write the fact here, short and plain, th: Write the fact here, short and plain, the way you would leave a note for a friend.
If an entry should be included every tim: If an entry should be included every time, keywords or not, set its status from **Normal** to **Constant**.
Short notes are cheaper. I like cheap. I: Short notes are cheaper. I like cheap. I mean, efficient.
Narrow it down with a filter: Narrow it down with a filter
**Optional Filter** is a second list of: **Optional Filter** is a second list of words that is checked after the keywords match. **Logic** decides what it needs.
**AND ANY** needs at least one filter wo: **AND ANY** needs at least one filter word as well. **AND ALL** needs every filter word. **NOT ANY** keeps the entry out if any filter word appears, and **NOT ALL** keeps it out only when all of them appear.
Leave the filter empty and only the keyw: Leave the filter empty and only the keywords count.
'Mara' with NOT ANY 'funeral' keeps her: 'Mara' with NOT ANY 'funeral' keeps her party plans out of the sad scene. I am a very sensitive cat.
Where it goes and who goes first: Where it goes and who goes first
**Position** picks where the entry sits: **Position** picks where the entry sits in what the model reads: before or after the character details, around the example messages or the Author's Note, or **@D** to place it inside the chat itself. **Outlet** holds it back for a prompt that asks for it.
**Depth** only matters for **@D**: 0 put: **Depth** only matters for **@D**: 0 puts it after the newest message, 4 puts it four messages back.
**Order** settles ties when several entr: **Order** settles ties when several entries land in the same place: higher numbers go closer to the end, where the model pays them more attention.
**Trigger probability** is the chance, o: **Trigger probability** is the chance, out of 100, that the entry joins in when its keywords match.
Depth 0 is shouting it in the model's ea: Depth 0 is shouting it in the model's ear. Use it for things that truly cannot be forgotten, like my snack schedule.
Everything in here is optional. The defa: Everything in here is optional. The defaults suit most entries, so only change what one entry really needs.
I have opened it for you. Press **Next**: I have opened it for you. Press **Next** and I will go through its three groups: **Activation rules**, **Inclusion and timing** and **Additional matching sources**.
The scary drawer. Do not worry, nothing: The scary drawer. Do not worry, nothing in here bites. Except me, occasionally.
When an entry joins in, its own text is: When an entry joins in, its own text is searched for keywords too, so one entry can wake another. This is called **recursion**, and it needs **Recursive Scan** switched on in the lorebook settings.
**Non-recursable** means other entries c: **Non-recursable** means other entries cannot wake this one. **Prevent further recursion** stops this one from waking others. **Delay until recursion** means only another entry can wake it, never the chat.
**Ignore budget** lets it in even when t: **Ignore budget** lets it in even when the lorebook space is full. **Agent blacklisted** hides it from Agents that look things up in your lorebooks.
A mentions B, B mentions C, and suddenly: A mentions B, B mentions C, and suddenly the whole family tree turns up for dinner. That is recursion.
**Selective** switches the Optional Filt: **Selective** switches the Optional Filter on or off, and **Use Probability** does the same for Trigger probability.
The boxes beside them replace a lorebook: The boxes beside them replace a lorebook-wide setting for this entry alone. Leave them on **Use global** unless this entry should behave differently.
**Scan Depth** is how many recent messag: **Scan Depth** is how many recent messages are searched for its keywords. **Case-Sensitive** and **Whole Words** change how exactly a keyword must match.
Whole Words on means 'cat' will not matc: Whole Words on means 'cat' will not match 'catastrophe'. Learned that one the hard way.
Entries with the same **Inclusion Group*: Entries with the same **Inclusion Group** name take turns: if several match at once, only one joins in. **Group Weight** makes one more likely to be picked, **Prioritize** lets it win outright, and **Group Scoring** picks the one with the most matching keywords.
**Sticky** keeps an entry in for that ma: **Sticky** keeps an entry in for that many messages after it wakes. **Cooldown** makes it sit out that many messages afterwards. **Delay** keeps it out until the chat has at least that many messages.
**Filter to Characters or Tags** limits: **Filter to Characters or Tags** limits the entry to the characters you list, or keeps it away from them with **Exclude**. **Filter to Generation Triggers** limits it to kinds of reply, such as swipes or continues.
Three moods for one character, one group: Three moods for one character, one group, and the model only ever sees one. Very tidy. Very unlike my room.
Keywords are normally only searched for: Keywords are normally only searched for in the chat messages. Tick any of these to also search the character's description, personality, scenario, notes or your persona.
Use it for an entry that should follow a: Use it for an entry that should follow a character around, whatever is being said.
Now the book can read the character shee: Now the book can read the character sheet too. Nosy, like me.
**Health** looks for problems, such as e: **Health** looks for problems, such as entries with no keywords, and offers fixes. The battery beside it shows how much of the model's reading space your always-included entries take up.
Free check-ups. The only free thing arou: Free check-ups. The only free thing around here, so enjoy it.
A book only works once it is switched on: A book only works once it is switched on. Choose it in this list to use it in every chat.
To tie a book to one character instead,: To tie a book to one character instead, open their card and press **Character Lore**.
A lorebook nobody switched on is just a: A lorebook nobody switched on is just a very well-organised diary. Mine is badly organised, but that is beside the point.
How much the lorebooks may add: How much the lorebooks may add
These settings apply to every lorebook a: These settings apply to every lorebook at once. **Scan Depth** is how many recent messages are searched for keywords.
**Context %** and **Budget Cap** limit h: **Context %** and **Budget Cap** limit how much of the model's reading space entries may take. When it is full, the rest are left out, so keep this in mind for big books.
**Min Activations** keeps searching furt: **Min Activations** keeps searching further back until at least that many entries have joined, but never past **Max Depth**. **Max Recursion Steps** limits how many times in a row entries may wake each other.
**Insertion Strategy** decides whether t: **Insertion Strategy** decides whether the character's own lorebook or the global ones go first.
A budget. For words. Even my lorebooks a: A budget. For words. Even my lorebooks are on a diet.
**Include Names** also searches the name: **Include Names** also searches the names of whoever is speaking. **Recursive Scan** lets entries wake other entries.
**Case Sensitive** and **Match Whole Wor: **Case Sensitive** and **Match Whole Words** set how exactly keywords must match; an entry can still choose its own. **Use Group Scoring** turns on group scoring everywhere.
**Alert On Overflow** warns you when ent: **Alert On Overflow** warns you when entries were left out because the budget was full.
Turn on the overflow alert. Silent failu: Turn on the overflow alert. Silent failures are how I lost three naps last week.

Neconyan does not write replies itself. It sends your chat to a **model**, an AI service that writes the reply, and this page decides which one.

Agents are saved prompts that run around: Agents are saved prompts that run around each reply. They can steer the reply before it is written, rewrite it afterwards, or keep notes of their own.
Taro can walk you through this page, one: Taro can walk you through this page, one step at a time.
An **agent** is a saved prompt with rule: An **agent** is a saved prompt with rules for when it runs, which model it uses and where its result goes.
A **prompt or reply** agent works on the: A **prompt or reply** agent works on the reply itself: it adds instructions before the reply is written, or changes the reply afterwards. A **companion** makes its own request after a reply and saves a separate note. It never replaces the reply.
Think of them as staff. Good staff, when: Think of them as staff. Good staff, when you tell them exactly what to do.
This line shows whether agents are runni: This line shows whether agents are running, how many you have, how many are switched on, and how many **prompt tokens** the switched-on agents add to each request. Tokens are the pieces of text models count.
**Agents On** pauses every agent at once: **Agents On** pauses every agent at once and keeps each agent’s own switch as it was. **Fix trackers** runs your tracker agents again on the last reply; trackers are agents that keep a running record, such as clothes, location or health. **Stop agent** appears only while an agent is running.
One switch to silence the lot. Use it be: One switch to silence the lot. Use it before you start blaming the model.

Use setups to swap between, say, a quiet: Use setups to swap between, say, a quiet setup for short chats and a full setup for long stories.

Your agent list is empty, so there is no: Your agent list is empty, so there is no card to show yet. Use **Browse library** or **Create agent** first.
Each card has a switch, shows when it ru: Each card has a switch, shows when it runs, and lists its main settings underneath.
Read the labels. They tell you most of t: Read the labels. They tell you most of the story without opening anything.

It can also change text written with Imp: It can also change text written with Impersonate, or companion notes before they are saved. Every change is kept in the message’s history, where you can compare the old and new text and undo it.
A proofreader that never sleeps. Check i: A proofreader that never sleeps. Check its work anyway.

Companions take notes. The reply stays y: Companions take notes. The reply stays yours.

Meowlcome~! Before anything else, you ne: Meowlcome~! Before anything else, you need something, that LLM thing, to connect to Neconyan before you can get to talk. This still feels like magic to me, I get so excited every single time!
Check **Connections** to select a provid: Check **Connections** to select a provider and paste your key in after deciding on the backend.
Take your time finding the key! I once w: Take your time finding the key! I once waited forty minutes waiting for the train at the other side, so… hehe. Tell me if it connects, I wanna cheer!
Now, who are we meeting? This is my favo: Now, who are we meeting? This is my favourite part, honestly! Create a character or import one, then choose Open chat, and if a line on the card reads wrong later, Edit card is where you change what is written on it.
Taro, Nori and I can draft a card or sug: Taro, Nori and I can draft a card or suggest an edit when your model supports tools, but we ask first and you approve every change; nothing is saved until you say so. I will still be excited about it, but I will wait until you say the magic word yes!
Four workspaces, each with one job: Role: Four workspaces, each with one job: Roleplay is the usual chat, Conversation is reminiscent of Signal and Telegram, Meower is a social media, and Story Mode gives you a co-writing interface.
Switch whenever you like, because your d: Switch whenever you like, because your draft survives the move; I expected it to, and then I checked, which is the order I prefer, and the order matters purr me. … Tell me that was funny.
A purrfect place for every detail: A purrfect place for every detail
That side character with the terrible se: That side character with the terrible secret deserves an address, so make a lorebook, then add entries with the keywords that should pull them into a scene; folders are how you find them again once the pile grows.
Back to library keeps your draft, and de: Back to library keeps your draft, and deleting a folder drops its books into Unfiled rather than the bin, so the character is out of my paper pile but still in the story. I would claim I invented libraries, but I am lying; the pile was here first.
Each agent has a job you specify, or pic: Each agent has a job you specify, or pick a built-in one created by our maker. I’m paw-sitive this will improve your roleplaying and writing experience. Check for any agents you might like, transfer the trackers to Companion if you so wish… just make sure to leave me some fish.
… Okay, I can explain better. They can c: … Okay, I can explain better. They can change your reply or run alongside the generation as extra context. Happy, hmm?
Neconyan has its own included tools and: Neconyan has its own included tools and extensions. You can see ‘em in the sidebar, no problem. The third-party extensions you install are in Extensions. Wow, who’da thunk?
Make sure to check first if any of the b: Make sure to check first if any of the bundled tools fit your purpose before scouring around for others. I’m territorial, you know… hehe, kidding!
Come in properly and put your cup down!: Come in properly and put your cup down!
Check the Appearance for ways to, well,: Check the Appearance for ways to, well, you guessed it, change the look of Neconyan. Don’t worry, you can change it any time!
If you want the kitty and the ears to st: If you want the kitty and the ears to stop moving, make sure to check Reduced Motion.
What’s your favourite colour? Mine’s ora: What’s your favourite colour? Mine’s orange! Maybe we can match~?
Change one setting, then look at what ha: Change one setting, then look at what happened before you change the next. Search finds a control by name, and Sampling shows which settings your provider and model will actually accept.
Turning every slider at once is a poor e: Turning every slider at once is a poor experiment, however satisfying, because you learn nothing about which one helped. Your saved sampler values stay put when you switch models.
You can replay the tour any time from Ho: You can replay the tour any time from Home → Home layout, and if you have any questions, come chat with any of us. We’re purr-eaty much available 24/7!
Connect, pick a character, chat. That’s: Connect, pick a character, chat. That’s the whole recipe; lorebooks, presets, Agents, Notebooks and the Scratchpad are in the sidebar whenever you want them. You can replay the tour any time from Home → Home layout.
When you feel like exploring, press **Sh: When you feel like exploring, press **Show all features** in the sidebar, or turn off Simple Mode in Settings → Appearance. Everything is still there, just napping.
Neconyan has a lot of buttons. Like, a l: Neconyan has a lot of buttons. Like, a lot. **Simple Mode** keeps the chat, your characters, your connection, presets, lorebooks, Agents, Notebooks and the Scratchpad, and tucks the rest away.
